name: flipoff
description: Free split-flap display emulator for any TV. The classic flip-board look, without the $3,500 hardware.
readme_summary: FlipOff is a free, open-source web application that emulates the look and feel of a classic mechanical split-flap display, commonly found in airports and train stations. It runs in a web browser, allowing users to turn any TV or monitor into a retro-style information board with realistic animations and sounds.
key_features: Realistic split-flap animation with scramble transitions
primary_use_case: To provide a free, browser-based emulation of a split-flap display for decorative or informational purposes on TVs and large monitors.
cover_image_prompt: A whimsical, retro-futuristic airport departure board room, where a large, vintage television screen is magically transforming into a classic split-flap display. Instead of physical flaps, the TV screen shows animated digital characters flipping and scrambling before settling on crisp text. Subtle digital particles and glowing data streams flow from a small, open laptop displaying the 'FlipOff' logo towards the TV, symbolizing the software's emulation. The room has a warm, inviting atmosphere with soft lighting, emphasizing the nostalgic yet digital nature of the display. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, friendly aesthetic.

name: teleop
description: Turns your phone or VR headset into a robot arm teleoperation device by leveraging WebXR
readme_summary: This repository enables teleoperation of robot arms using a phone or VR headset through a web interface powered by WebXR. It translates device orientation and position data into robot control commands, supporting various robot interfaces and ROS 2 integration.
key_features: WebXR-based teleoperation via phone or VR headset
Python server for receiving device data
Support for ROS 2 cartesian_controllers, MoveIt Servo, and IK solutions
Customizable interfaces using the Teleop class
primary_use_case: Enabling intuitive, wireless teleoperation of robot arms using readily available mobile devices or VR headsets.
cover_image_prompt: A person's hand holding a smartphone, which is projecting a holographic beam of light that precisely guides a robotic arm in a clean, modern workshop. The smartphone screen displays simple, intuitive controls like 'Start' and 'Move', with subtle glowing lines connecting it to the robot's end effector. The robotic arm is shown in mid-motion, performing a delicate task. In the background, a subtle data stream visualization flows, hinting at the underlying technology. The overall mood is futuristic and empowering, emphasizing seamless control. The art style should be a 3D isometric illustration with vibrant, clean colors and clear, defined lines.

name: eventum
description: Realistic synthetic events for testing, demos, and pipelines — streamed live or generated in bulk
readme_summary: Eventum is a Python-based data generation platform that creates realistic synthetic events for testing, demos, and data pipelines. It supports streaming events live or generating them in bulk, with flexible scheduling and multiple output destinations.
key_features: Realistic data generation using Faker and Mimesis
Multiple output destinations (stdout, files, ClickHouse, OpenSearch, HTTP)
Real-time streaming and bulk generation modes
MCP server for AI assistant integration
primary_use_case: Generating realistic synthetic event data for testing, demonstrations, and data pipelines.
cover_image_prompt: A master craftsman in a bustling workshop, meticulously assembling intricate clockwork gears that represent diverse data types (logs, user events, network traffic). These gears are fed into a large, stylized funnel labeled 'Eventum', which then streams out perfectly formed, glowing data packets into various destinations: a database icon, a file cabinet, and a live network stream. Subtle digital particles and UI elements showing schedules and data previews float around the scene. The overall mood is one of precision and controlled creation. The style should be a vibrant 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a focus on clear visual storytelling.

name: CraftHub
description: CraftHub features a powerful JSON editor and JSON creation tools, alongside an intuitive platform for uploading existing programming language classes or building new ones from scratch.
readme_summary: CraftHub is a C# application built with Avalonia for .NET, offering robust tools for managing programming language classes and generating/comparing JSON data. It allows users to upload or create classes, save them, and then use these structures to easily generate and export JSON, with advanced features for comparing multiple JSON files.
key_features: JSON Comparison (document changes and multi-file comparison)
Configurable difference detection (key order, array order, case, nulls, specific paths)
Exportable comparison reports (patch, JSON Patch, HTML/Markdown)
primary_use_case: To provide a user-friendly interface for managing programming language class definitions and facilitating the creation, export, and comparison of JSON data structures.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan in a workshop meticulously crafting intricate gears and blueprints representing programming classes. One hand holds a glowing blueprint, while the other guides a stream of digital particles that form perfectly structured JSON documents on a workbench. In the background, a large, stylized 'JSON' symbol is being assembled. Subtle UI elements showing class definitions and JSON structures are visible on a nearby screen. The overall mood is one of creation and precision, with a clean, modern aesthetic. The image should be in a 3D isometric illustration style with vibrant, contrasting colors and clear, defined lines, emphasizing the transformation of abstract code into structured data.
